text: GAD-7 Generalised Anxiety Disorder screening tool. 7 item validated instrument for screening and severity measurement of generalised anxiety disorder. Scored 0 to 3 per item same as PHQ-9. Total score 0 to 21. Severity thresholds: 5 to 9 mild monitor reassess in 2 weeks. 10 to 14 moderate likely anxiety disorder consider treatment refer to GP. 15 to 21 severe active anxiety disorder refer urgently consider medication and CBT. Depression and anxiety are highly comorbid. Approximately 50 percent of patients with MDD also meet criteria for an anxiety disorder. Pharmacist Note: Administer alongside PHQ-9 for comprehensive screening.

Insomnia assessment and management in pharmacy setting. Insomnia definition: difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep or non restorative sleep causing significant distress or functional impairment lasting more than one month. Short term insomnia less than 3 months often situational. Chronic insomnia more than 3 months requires investigation. Common causes: anxiety depression stress poor sleep hygiene caffeine alcohol medications including steroids beta blockers stimulants. Pharmacist Assessment Questions: How long have you had sleep problems. What happens when you cannot sleep. Do you feel anxious or worried at night. Are you tired during the day. What medications and supplements are you taking. Pharmacist Action: Screen for underlying depression or anxiety using PHQ-9 and GAD-7 before recommending any sleep aid.

OTC sleep aids available in pharmacy. Antihistamine based sleep aids diphenhydramine promethazine. Suitable for short term occasional use only maximum 2 weeks. Not suitable for chronic insomnia. Tolerance develops quickly. Not suitable for elderly patients increased fall risk. Not suitable for patients with urinary retention glaucoma. Melatonin available OTC in some regions. More physiological approach. Better evidence for circadian rhythm issues jet lag shift work. Herbal options valerian passionflower limited evidence. Pharmacist Caution: Before recommending any OTC sleep aid always ask about current medications supplements including herbal products. Screen for depression and anxiety. Ask about alcohol use. St Johns Wort interaction must be checked.

Mild anxiety management in community pharmacy. For patients presenting with mild anxiety symptoms GAD-7 score 5 to 9 with no current treatment and symptoms less than 6 weeks. First line non pharmacological approaches: sleep hygiene advice, caffeine reduction, regular exercise, relaxation techniques, guided self help CBT based apps such as Headspace Calm or NHS recommended apps. Pharmacist can advise on all of the above without GP referral for mild cases. Refer to GP if: symptoms persist beyond 6 weeks, GAD-7 score 10 or above, patient also has depressive symptoms, patient is already on medication for anxiety, patient requests formal diagnosis or treatment.
